facts.statement: Callawayia is an extinct genus of ichthyosaur.
facts.quote: Callawayia is an extinct genus of ichthyosaur.

facts.statement: Callawayia was a small ichthyosaur that grew to a length of 2 to 2.5 meters.
facts.quote: Callawayia is a small ichthyosaur measuring 2 - 2.5 m long.

facts.statement: Callawayia possessed large frontals, which are a pair of skull roof bones.
facts.quote: The frontals (a pair of skull roof bones) of Callawayia are large.

facts.statement: Callawayia had over 54 vertebrae located in front of its hips.
facts.quote: Callawayia has a total of over 54 vertebrae in front of its hips.

facts.statement: The cervical ribs of Callawayia were double-headed, distinguishing them from the single-headed ribs found behind them.
facts.quote: The cervical (neck) ribs are double-headed, unlike the single-headed ribs behind them.

facts.statement: The scapulae of Callawayia featured long and narrow shafts.
facts.quote: The scapulae have long, narrow shafts.

facts.statement: In Callawayia, the small opening known as an obturator foramen on each pubic bone was not entirely enclosed by bone.
facts.quote: Each pubic bone (front lower hip bone) bears a small opening known as an obturator foramen which, in Callawayia, is not entirely enclosed by bone.

facts.statement: Callawayia possessed short, wide humeri with notched front edges.
facts.quote: The short, wide humeri (upper arm bones) have notched front edges.

facts.statement: Callawayia had four digits in its foreflippers and only three digits in its hindflippers.
facts.quote: There are four digits in the foreflippers, while the hindflippers have only three.

facts.statement: An additional bone known as a pisiform was present in each foreflipper of Callawayia.
facts.quote: An additional bone, known as a pisiform, is present in each foreflipper.

facts.statement: The genus Callawayia was described by Maisch and Matzke in 2000.
facts.quote: authority: Maisch & Matzke, 2000

facts.statement: The type species of Callawayia is Callawayia neoscapularis, originally named as Shastasaurus neoscapularis by McGowan in 1994.
facts.quote: subdivision: * Callawayia neoscapularis McGowan, 1994 (type) [originally Shastasaurus]

facts.statement: Callawayia is classified within the family Shastasauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Shastasauridae

facts.statement: Callawayia lived during the Late Triassic period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Triassic,

facts.statement: Fossils of Callawayia date from the Norian stage of the Late Triassic, between 227.3 and 205.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Norian (227.3 to 205.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: Fossils of Callawayia have been found in what is now Canada.
facts.quote: Se han encontrado en lo que ahora es Canadá.

facts.statement: The species Callawayia neoscapularis was originally based on a partial skeleton discovered in 1987 on the shore of Williston Lake in Pink Mountain, British Columbia, Canada.
facts.quote: based on ROM (Royal Ontario Museum) 41993, a partial skeleton discovered on the shore of Williston Lake in Pink Mountain, British Columbia, Canada in 1987.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Callawayia neoscapularis was excavated from the "Flipper Quarry" in 1988.
facts.quote: The specimen was excavated from "Flipper Quarry" in 1988.

facts.statement: The genus Callawayia was named in honor of the ichthyosaur researcher Jack Callaway.
facts.quote: named a new genus, Callawayia, named in honor of ichthyosaur researcher Jack Callaway

facts.statement: A new species, Callawayia wolonggangense, was named in 2007 based on material found in Guizhou, China.
facts.quote: In 2007, X. Chen and colleagues named a new species of Callawayia, C. wolonggangse, based on material from Guizhou, China.

facts.statement: Nicholls and Manabe considered the naming of Callawayia unethical because the authors were aware that a study naming a different genus was in progress.
facts.quote: Nicholls and Manabe, while acknowledging that Callawayia was the correct name, considered its naming unethical, based on the International Code of Zoological Nomenclature's Code of Ethics

facts.statement: In 2016, Ji and colleagues rejected the assignment of Callawayia wolonggangense to the genus Callawayia because they found no characteristics uniting it with the type species.
facts.quote: In 2016, Ji and colleagues found no characteristics uniting "C." wolonggangense and the type species of Callawayia, C. neoscapularis, and thus rejected the assignment of the former species to this genus.

facts.statement: Ji and colleagues also rejected assigning Callawayia wolonggangense to the genus Guizhouichthyosaurus due to a lack of unambiguous linking traits.
facts.quote: However, they found no traits unambiguously linking it to Guizhouichthyosaurus either, thus also rejected its assignment to that genus.

facts.statement: The species name neoscapularis refers to the fact that its shoulder blades resemble those of Jurassic ichthyosaurs more than those of other Triassic ichthyosaurs.
facts.quote: The name of this species refers to the closer resemblance of its scapulae (shoulder blades) to Jurassic ichthyosaurs than those of other Triassic ichthyosaurs.
